---
title: "Download the FFB checklist"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `flora_download()` function of the `floraR` package. This function downloads taxonomic and distributional records from the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) platform in Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) format, directly from the [FFB IPT data portal](https://ipt.jbrj.gov.br/jbrj/resource?r=lista_especies_flora_brasil).

## Function Overview

`flora_download()` retrieves one or more versions of the FFB dataset and saves each one to its own subdirectory on disk. It checks whether a requested version is already present locally and avoids re-downloading it unnecessarily, so it is safe to call repeatedly across a project.

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `version` | Character. `"latest"` (default) downloads the most recent release; `"all"` downloads every available version (large!); a version string or vector of version strings (e.g. `"393.418"`) downloads specific releases. Use `flora_version()` to inspect valid version numbers first. |
| `verbose` | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints informative messages during download. |
| `dir` | Character. Local directory to save the downloaded files. Defaults to `"flora_download"`. Each version is extracted into its own subdirectory. |

## Download the latest dataset

```r
library(floraR)

flora_download(dir = "flora_download")
```

## Download a specific version

Use [`flora_version()`](/articles/check_ffb_versions.qmd) first to find a valid version string:

```r
versions_df <- flora_version()

flora_download(version = versions_df$Version[1], dir = "flora_download")
```

## Download multiple versions

```r
flora_download(version = c("393.418", "392.417"), dir = "flora_download")
```

## Download every available version

```r
# Large download! Only needed for archival or cross-version comparisons.
flora_download(version = "all", dir = "flora_download")
```

## Additional Tips

- You rarely need to call `flora_download()` directly: `flora_records()`, `flora_search()`, `flora_match()`, and `flora_get_children_taxa()` all download and cache the dataset automatically the first time you call them.
- If no internet connection is available, `flora_download()` automatically falls back to a previously downloaded local copy, if one exists in `dir`.
- Keep the downloaded folder (the default `rm_flora_database = FALSE` behavior in downstream functions) so that repeated analyses reuse the cache instead of re-downloading the archive every time.
